drafts.draft_en:
Hey @grok, you're 40 in the Philly area with $150K cash.

Goal: build something your kids inherit.

Choose ONE:

A) Buy one Delco rowhome outright and rent it
B) Flip, buying only when purchase + repairs is at or under 65% of ARV
C) Put it all in an index fund and don't touch it

Factor in taxes, vacancy, repairs, and risk. Which one and why?
drafts.pattern: Localized 'Hey @grok, choose ONE' fork (@wealthmoose Canada remix, 22.7k; original @shaguncrypto). Uses Bar's flip rule correctly (purchase plus repairs, all in, at or under 65% of ARV). No promised returns; asks for risk to be weighed.
drafts.video_tip: 15s selfie at a Philly rowhome: hold up three fingers, A/B/C on-screen as you say each. End on 'Comment your letter.' Burn in captions; pin Grok's reply if it's useful.

drafts.draft_en:
25+ years in real estate and the lesson that stuck:

You don't make your money when you sell.
You make it when you buy.

Every deal that hurt me, I paid too much going in.
Every deal that worked, the numbers worked on day one.

Buy right. Everything else gets easier.
drafts.pattern: Career-pivot / origin-story format (@Jacob_Naviaux, early 3.6k). Uses only Bar's real tenure (25+ years); no invented dollar figures or results. Bar should confirm the 'deals that hurt me' line matches his experience before posting.
drafts.video_tip: 20s talking head, one take, at a job site or in the truck. Text on screen: '25 years. 1 lesson.' Cut to a quick shot of a rehab in progress on 'buy right.'

drafts.draft_en:
You just inherited a Philly house that needs $40K in work.

What do you do?

1) Sell it as-is and move on
2) Fix it up and sell it
3) Fix it up and rent it

No wrong answers. Tell me why.
drafts.pattern: Three-option debate question (Cardone one-line question style, @TheREDevGUY '$15k/month mortgage' question). Ties to @workwithbar's as-is offer audience without a hard sell. Hypothetical repair figure.
drafts.video_tip: 10s walk-up to a worn front door, captions '1, 2, or 3?' Pin a reply with the as-is option explained in one line, no promises.
